security_privacy_cost_impact: data classification synthetic-only; secrets required false; network policy deny-unless-declared. Documentation only: one RFC, one Owner disposition, three one-line registrations and one manifest entry. No contract, fixture, test, credential, provider call, migration or customer-data effect. The RFC, once accepted and landed, narrows what a metric label may carry, which keeps correlation ids and fine-grained codes out of metric labels. Cost: the RFC proposes an upper bound of 24,480 series per metric per environment; nothing is emitted today and the standing restriction (no sli_tags to a real metric backend before the budget lands) is unchanged.
migration_and_data_impact: None. No migration, database object or persisted data is touched; Gate G0 forbids them.
compatibility_impact: Additive. No contract schema, fixture or status changes in this increment, so no accepted set moves. RFC-2026-033 §7 classifies the later §8 edits: both enums narrow CTR-OBS-001 (breaking by RFC-2026-031 §3.3's definition, not bound by it at Candidate), rejecting only the accepted-gap fixture; that increment carries the change and its own round.
